# Claude Code Permission Modes

A permission mode sets which tool calls run without a prompt.
The modes go from `plan`, which only reads, to `bypassPermissions`, which skips most checks.
For example, `claude --permission-mode acceptEdits` starts a session that edits files with no prompt.
The marks are explained on [Permissions and Sandbox](Claude-Code-Permissions-And-Sandbox).

## The Six Modes

The list in the bundle is `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `bypassPermissions`, `default`, `dontAsk`, `plan`.
The word `manual` is an alias of `default`.
The error text is `Cannot set permission mode: must be one of acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, default, dontAsk, plan`.

| Mark | Item | What It Does | How It Works | Where It Can Be Used | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✅ | `default` | Standard behavior | Prompts for dangerous operations. The picker text is `default (ask each time)` | `--permission-mode`, `defaultMode`, `/permissions` | [Configure Permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), [Choose a Permission Mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes) |
| ✅ | `acceptEdits` | Auto-accepts file edits | Picker text: `accept edits (auto-approve file edits and common file commands)`. It allows edits inside the workspace. A Bash check says `would be allowed in acceptEdits mode` | Same | [Configure Permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), [Choose a Permission Mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes) |
| ✅ | `plan` | Analysis only, no edits | Picker text: `plan mode (research and propose changes without making them)`. With auto mode available, plan mode uses auto mode semantics unless `useAutoModeDuringPlan` is `false` | Same | [Configure Permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), [Choose a Permission Mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes) |
| ✅ | `auto` | A classifier screens each action | Picker text: `auto (no routine prompts, a reviewer model screens actions)`. See [Auto Mode](Claude-Code-Permissions-And-Sandbox-Auto-Mode) | Same. Not from project or local `defaultMode` | [Configure Permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), [Choose a Permission Mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes) |
| ✅ | `dontAsk` | Denies what would prompt | Picker text: `don't ask (auto-deny anything that would prompt)`. The deny reason says `Claude Code is running in don't ask mode` | Same | [Configure Permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), [Choose a Permission Mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes) |
| ✅ | `bypassPermissions` | Skips permission checks | Picker text: `BYPASS PERMISSIONS (no further prompts)`. Explicit `deny` rules still apply. Safety checks marked bypass-immune still ask | Needs `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`. Not from project or local `defaultMode` | [Configure Permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), [Choose a Permission Mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes) |

## Rules for Choosing and Cycling a Mode

- `permissions.defaultMode` sets the start mode.
  `--permission-mode` wins for one session.
  Source: `settings.md`.
- The values `auto` and `bypassPermissions` are modes that project and local settings cannot set.
  Source: bundle.
- `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` and an unaccepted bypass dialog stop `bypassPermissions`.
  The bundle texts are `bypassPermissions mode is disabled by settings` and `Cannot set permission mode to bypassPermissions because the session was not launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions`.
- A cloud session cannot use `bypassPermissions`.
  Source: bundle error text.
- The bundle list of modes in the cycle for the IDE host is `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `default`, `auto`.
  The order in the terminal is not documented.

## Decision Reason Types

Each decision has a `decisionReason` with one of these types.
Source: the bundle.

| Mark | Item | What It Does | How It Works | Where It Can Be Used | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🔍 | `rule` | A permission rule decided | Text such as `Denied by a permission rule` | Each tool | bundle |
| 🔍 | `mode` | The mode decided | For example `dontAsk` denies | Each tool | bundle |
| 🔍 | `subcommandResults` | Parts of a compound command decided | Each sub-command has its own reason | `Bash`, `PowerShell` | bundle |
| 🔍 | `permissionPromptTool` | An MCP permission prompt tool decided | Set with `--permission-prompt-tool` | Print mode | bundle |
| 🔍 | `hook` | A hook decided | `PreToolUse` or `PermissionRequest` | Hooks | bundle |
| 🔍 | `asyncAgent` | A background agent has no prompt surface | Denies with `no approval surface in this session` | Background agents | bundle |
| 🔍 | `sandboxOverride` | A command runs outside the sandbox | The text is `Run outside of the sandbox` | `Bash` | bundle |
| 🔍 | `workingDir` | The path is outside the working directories | Text `Path is outside allowed working directories` | File tools | bundle |
| 🔍 | `safetyCheck` | A built-in safety check fired | See the next table | Each tool | bundle |
| 🔍 | `classifier` | The auto mode classifier decided | Text `Denied by auto mode classifier` or `Allowed by auto mode classifier` | `auto` mode | bundle |
| 🔍 | `other` | Anything else | For example a closed permission stream | Hosts | bundle |

## Safety Checks (Circuit Breakers)

A `safetyCheck` carries a `circuitBreaker` name.
The flags tell if the check is immune to `bypassPermissions` (`bypassImmune`), goes to the classifier (`classifierRouted`), or only a person may answer (`hostPersonOnly`).
Source: the bundle.

| Mark | Item | What It Does | How It Works | Where It Can Be Used | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🔍 | `dangerousRemoval` | Critical-path `rm` prompts | Bypass-immune, classifier-routed. A time limit applies unless `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DANGEROUS_RM_TIMEOUT=1` | `Bash` | bundle, `env.md` |
| 🔍 | `backgroundOperator` | Background operator calls | Classifier-routed | Background sessions | bundle |
| 🔍 | `suspiciousWindowsPath` | Odd Windows paths | Classifier-routed | Windows | bundle |
| ✅ | `isolatePeerMachines` | Peer machine isolation | Bypass-immune. Setting `isolatePeerMachines` | Managed | [Choose a Permission Mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes), [Settings Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference) |
| 🔍 | `restrictedMode` | `--restricted` | Bypass-immune | CLI | bundle |
| 🔍 | `outsideReadsBlocked` | `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` | Bypass-immune | File tools, `Bash` | bundle |
| 🔍 | `claudeSettingsFile` | Writes to settings files | Only a person answers | File tools | bundle |
| 🔍 | `internalHardDeny` | Built-in hard deny | Cannot be placed on a served classifier | Each tool | bundle |
| 🔍 | `unfinishedCheck` | A check did not finish | Bypass-immune, person only | Each tool | bundle |

## Decision Flow

The bundle shows these steps.
The docs do not give the full order.

1. Explicit `deny` and `ask` rules apply first.
   They apply before workspace trust.
   Source: `settings.md`.
2. `PreToolUse` hooks can allow, deny, or ask.
   A hook `allow` does not override a `deny` or `ask` rule.
   Source: `types-2.1.303.d.ts` and the bundle text `hook allows approve the command`.
3. `allow` rules, the `acceptEdits` rules, and read-only command lists allow the call.
   Bundle texts: `Read-only command is allowed`, `Auto-allowed with sandbox (autoAllowBashIfSandboxed enabled)`.
4. Otherwise the mode decides.
   `default` prompts, `dontAsk` denies, `auto` asks the classifier, `bypassPermissions` allows.
5. A prompt runs the `PermissionRequest` hooks first.
   Then the dialog shows.
   `Notification` hooks fire for unanswered requests in SDK hosts (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_PERMISSION_PROMPT_NOTIFY_HOOKS=1` stops that).
6. An auto mode denial fires `PermissionDenied`.
